title: Falcon 9 USSF-380 (SLC-4E)

azimuth_deg.derived: Great-circle bearing from the LL2 SLC-4E pad to the midpoint of the downrange edge of NAVAREA XII 836/26 Area A (hazardous rocket launching, USSF-380). Edge vertices 32-05.00N 119-08.00W and 32-30.00N 119-18.00W. Midpoint 32.2917N 119.2167W. Unrounded bearing 153.184 deg, rounded to 153.18. Distance 290.6 km. Non-rotating inclination 68.21 deg. Areas B and C of the same notice are further downrange (centroid bearings about 154.32 and 155.11 deg) and were not used. No ZLA CARF polygon for 29 Nov 2026 was retrieved. This Area A polygon is the same shape USSF-317 recorded for NAVAREA XII 785/26 and did not use; it is used here because it is the notice in force for this flight.

payload_kg.note: FITTED inside the Falcon 9 config bounds (13.0-21.6 t, themselves a Starlink V2 mini band) so the BORROWED SECO-1 time can reach the BORROWED parking altitude. USSF-380 mass is unpublished. The fitted number is an ASSUMPTION of the fit, not an estimate of the payload. No satellite count is used.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: USSF-380 orbit is unpublished. 177.3 km perigee is borrowed from the Starlink Group 15 parking orbit used for USSF-317. LL2 says this flight's drop zones match previous Starlink Group 15 launches, and the published times through SES-1 match the sl-15-16 family timeline that produced that orbit (MECO 2:26, SES-1 2:36, SECO-1 8:39). Fairing here is 2:57, one second later than that family's 2:56. It is not a USSF-380 element. Inclination is not tuned; the 153.18 deg hazard azimuth stands.

apoapsis_alt_km.assumption: Same borrowed Group 15 parking apogee used for USSF-317. Not a USSF-380 source.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude

header_notes: ILLUSTRATIVE. PRE-FLIGHT. USSF-380, Falcon 9, SLC-4E. T0 is the window open 2026-11-29T04:39:00Z (Sat 28 Nov 8:39 p.m. PT). SpaceX https://www.spacex.com/launches/ussf380 header: 28 Nov 23:39 ET to 29 Nov 03:39 ET, a four-hour window to 08:39Z. Backup Sun 29 Nov 6:26 p.m. PT = 2026-11-30T02:26:00Z. 27th flight of the first stage. Landing on Of Course I Still Love You. LL2 id b0d27def-0a88-44c3-a947-1fd5b8503e2c status Go at 04:39Z, window 04:39-08:39Z, last_updated 2026-11-26T11:45:38Z.

Published timeline (SpaceX ussf380): Max-Q 1:07, MECO 2:26, stage sep 2:29, SES-1 2:36, fairing 2:57, entry burn 6:04-6:27, landing burn 8:02, landing 8:25. SECO, orbit and deploy are not published. Payload is classified. No unofficial satellite count is used. SpaceX does not name the booster.

INFERRED/ASSUMED: SECO-1 at T+519 s and a 177.3 x 266.2 km parking orbit are borrowed from the Group 15 / USSF-317 config, not from USSF-380. LL2's mission text says the drop zones match previous Starlink Group 15 launches. File ends 2 revs after cutoff (deploy unpublished). Booster entry and landing are not modelled.

final_cutoff_s.assumption: USSF-380 SECO-1 is unpublished. T+8:39 is borrowed from https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-15-16 because MECO and SES-1 on the USSF-380 page match that timeline. Fairing here is 2:57, one second later than sl-15-16's 2:56. Stage separation here is 2:29, one second earlier than sl-15-16's 2:30.

knots.src: https://github.com/shahar603/Telemetry-Data/tree/master/Iridium%20NEXT%207 (SpaceX webcast telemetry; FAMILY stand-in, not this flight). This flight's published MECO is also T+146 s.
same. This flight's published SES-1 is also T+156 s.
same. This flight's published fairing separation is T+177 s, one second later; the family sample stays at T+176 s.

cd.assumption: same Cd as the ascent fit (fixed 0.4)

deploy.note: SpaceX publishes no SECO, restart or deploy time for USSF-380 (classified payload). Propagated 2 revs on the inferred insertion orbit. The insertion altitude is borrowed, not a USSF-380 element.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 27 V2 Mini Optimized: ~575 kg each community-reported (spacex.com.pl) = 15.5 t; MaxQ lists 800 kg each = 21.6 t (upper bound). Mass not published by SpaceX
